teaching.causalExplanation: Start with the cereal box from last time. If you slice straight across it, every slice is the same rectangle, twenty centimetres by eight. That slice shape is called the cross-section. Stack those slices along the box's thirty centimetre length, and you've filled it. So the volume is the area of the end, a hundred and sixty square centimetres, times the length, thirty. That's forty-eight hundred cubic centimetres, which is four point eight litres. This works for any prism, any solid that's the same shape all the way through. Volume equals the area of the end, times the length. In symbols, V equals A h. Notice the box needed two thousand square centimetres of cardboard, but holds forty-eight hundred cubic centimetres. Different question, different units. The end doesn't have to be a rectangle. This entrance ramp is solid concrete. From the side, it's a right-angled triangle, five point six metres along the ground and rising nought point four of a metre. That triangle stays the same all the way across the ramp, which is one point five metres wide. So the end is the triangle, and the length it runs for is the width, one point five. The triangle's area is half of five point six times nought point four, one point one two square metres. Times one point five gives one point six eight cubic metres of concrete. Multiplying the three measurements together, and forgetting the half, would order twice as much concrete as you need. Back to the tank. A cylinder is a prism with a circle at each end, so its end is a circle, and its length is its height. The tank is one point eight metres wide, so the radius is nought point nine. The circle's area is pi times nought point nine squared. Times the height, two, that's one point six two pi, about five point nought nine cubic metres. Every cubic metre is a kilolitre, so the tank holds about five point nought nine kilolitres, around five thousand and ninety litres. For a cylinder, V equals pi r squared h. Halve the diameter first, and keep every measurement in metres before you multiply.

scenes.teachingReason: Composite solids work by adding or taking away, just like composite shapes. A concrete drainage pipe is a cylinder with a smaller cylinder missing from the middle. Its outer radius is nought point five metres, its hole has a radius of nought point four, and it's two metres long. Its end is a ring, the outer circle minus the inner circle.
